comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-24: fixed on main in 8e826635, with a test that failed before the fix. Each command that refuses --window says what it does without it; the reopen hint stays only on window reopen. Hiding --window from those commands' help needs the CLI to build its clap command by hand; not done.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-22 on 0.18.0, laptop. `muster msg post --to <pane> --window window-6 "..."` was refused: "--window window-6 names the window a command is about, and this command is not about one window, so nothing was done. `muster window reopen window-6` brings a closed window back." window-6 was open, with 16 panes in `muster window list`, so the reopen hint pointed the wrong way. `msg post --help` lists `--window` among its options, which is why it was passed. Without `--window` the post found the pane on its own.

`for_window` in `crates/muster-cli/src/args.rs` gives the reopen hint on every refusal: for every command that is not about one window, whether the named window is open or closed.

Possibly: give the reopen hint only when the named window is closed, and otherwise say the command finds its targets across windows without `--window`. If help can be shaped per command, leave `--window` out of the help of commands that refuse it.
title: msg post --window on an open window says to reopen it
